title: War-driven high energy prices expected to ease global fossil fuel emissions
description: War-driven high energy prices expected to ease global fossil fuel emissions Emissions are projected to ease by 0.4% from the previous year’s record level to 38.2 billion metric tonnes of carbon dioxide, the Global Carbon Project said. Tuesday 10/11/2026 LONDON Global fossil fuel carbon emissions are set to fall this year, because of high energy prices and increased use of renewable power, though it is too soon to say they have peaked, a consortium of international scientists said on Tuesday. Emissions are projected to ease by 0.4% from the previous year’s record level to 38.2 billion metric tonnes of carbon dioxide, the Global Carbon Project said. Scientists who contributed to the report said that renewable energy deployment needed to accelerate to send carbon emissions into more definite decline. “A drop in emissions in one year is not a peak unless it is driven by structural change,” Glen Peters, research professor at the CICERO Centre for International Climate Research, said. The report, produced by an international team of more than 140 scientists, found that emissions from oil had fallen by 1.9% this year, mainly because of the supply disruption caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, which drove energy prices higher, curbing demand. Emissions from natural gas are projected to fall 0.3% versus last year, while coal emissions are expected to rise by 0.6%, according to the report. China, the world’s largest carbon dioxide emitter, is expected to register a 0.9% fall in its emissions, while from the US, the world’s second-largest overall emitter, emissions are projected to drop by 1.3% versus the previous year.

title: Global Fossil Fuel Emissions Projected To Fall 0.4 Percent In 2026 Report
description: New projections indicate global fossil fuel emissions will drop 0.4 percent in 2026. The Global Carbon Project attributes this decline to clean energy expansion and geopolitical disruptions affecting energy markets.
